newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says president resting on doctors' orders.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says president resting on doctors' orders.

text.p: Vietnamese President Le Duc Anh, in hospital following a stroke last month, is resting on doctors' orders, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Thursday.

"President Le Duc Anh is in a recovery process, however the president still has to continue resting at the request of his medical doctor," the spokesman, Tran Quang Hoan, said at a news briefing for foreign journalists.
Anh, who turned 76 on Sunday, was admitted to a Hanoi hospital in mid-November suffering blood pressure problems.

But a veil of secrecy has been drawn across details of his condition. Medical sources speak of Anh, a member of Vietnam's leadership triumvirate, being only semi-conscious, while official statements on his health have been ambiguous.
Under Vietnam's constitution Anh's duties would be transferred to the vice-president if he were incapacitated for any length of time.

So far, however, there has been no announcement of any change and state media reported on Thursday that Anh sent a message on Wednesday to United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan.
Diplomats have said, however that Anh is not expected to be able to resume his duties.

Anh, a general, is viewed as a powerful behind-the-scenes operator and wields influence over the military. Analysts say his departure from the political scene could precipitate broader changes among the leadership.
